deck.topic: Texas market reality check: hidden discounts and the two speed market
deck.hook: Texas has 7 months of inventory. That number is lying.

points.title: The 7 Month Lie
body: Texas is sitting on roughly seven months of supply statewide.
On paper that reads like a buyer's market.
Almost all of that pile is stacked in the upper price bands.

points.title: The Discount Is Hidden
body: Sellers hate a public price cut. It sits on the record forever.
So they hold the list price and pay you a different way.
Closing costs, rate buydowns, repairs credited back at the table.
points.loop: Not every seller will do it.

points.title: Two Speeds, One Market
body: Correctly priced homes are still going under contract inside two weeks.
Everything else is sitting past ninety days and going stale.
There is almost no middle left.

points.title: Your First Two Weeks
body: Nearly every showing you will get is crammed into the first fourteen days.
Overprice it and you spend that window teaching buyers to scroll past you.
The price cut you make later never wins that traffic back.

points.title: Sellers Who Cannot Wait
body: The real bargains right now are people who already closed on their next house.
They are covering two payments and counting weeks, not months.
None of that ever shows up in the listing.
points.loop: How many depends on your ZIP.

linkedinCaption:
Texas is carrying roughly seven months of supply statewide. That reads like a buyer's market until you look at where the inventory actually sits. Most of it is stacked in the upper price bands.

Meanwhile, correctly priced homes are still going under contract inside two weeks. Everything else is aging past ninety days. The middle has mostly disappeared.

The concessions are real, but they are quiet. Sellers resist public price cuts because the record follows the listing. They pay through closing costs, rate buydowns, and repair credits instead. None of that shows up in the list price.

The strongest leverage comes from sellers already carrying two homes.

For the agents here: are you seeing concessions replace price reductions in your market too?
